_comment: Machine source for RNVizion identity facts, the sibling of engine/brand.py. Brand tokens are colors and type; these are the facts about the person and the products. Same rule applies: import it, never hardcode. Change a fact HERE first, then run refresh_profile.py --all to find every surface that disagrees. ARCHIVES: docs/eval-history/ preserves dated eval reports and must keep retired phrases verbatim; retirement checks skip it wholesale via ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE in refresh_profile.py, and the ledger prints that exclusion every sweep. No per-phrase exemptions are needed there, ever -- if a future retirement fails under docs/eval-history/, the checker regressed; do not add an exemption to quiet it.

identity._comment: Contact and handles. Byte-identical everywhere they appear.
identity.name: Christian Smith

role_emails._comment: Domain role addresses on rnvizion.dev, receive-only through Cloudflare Email Routing and forwarded to identity.email. The contact check recognizes these so they do not read as drift. identity.email stays canonical for resumes and applications until a send path passes DMARC in a recipient's headers. CORRECTED 2026-08-09: an earlier note here said consumer send-as cannot align. It does -- Yahoo sets envelope-from to the domain address, so the identifier was aligned all along and only the sending IP was unauthorized; one SPF include closed it. What remains is that DKIM still signs d=yahoo.com, so alignment rests on SPF alone and does not survive forwarding: fine for p=none and p=quarantine, not for p=reject.
role_emails.inquiries@rnvizion.dev: public contact; site contact section and bio
role_emails.dmarc@rnvizion.dev: DMARC aggregate reports; not published anywhere

email_change_coupling._comment: Changing identity.email is NOT a repo-only edit. One occurrence is an ownership claim served to a third party and verified against an account held there, so it changes on both sides or it breaks. Recorded because check_contact sees the string and cannot see the constraint on editing it.

facts._comment: Values on more than one surface that have drifted before. 'sources' are files the checker reads; 'appears_in' is the wider map including surfaces it cannot reach. 'match' is the literal phrase that must appear on those sources -- a bare value is a useless needle ("60" matches a CSS font weight), so where a fact is printed inside a phrase, give the phrase. MOVE 'match' WITH 'value': a stale match fails loudly on the next run, which is correct but surprising if you forget the pairing.

derive.note: Source 'def test_' count is a floor: parametrized tests expand at runtime. The checker verifies the displayed floor is actually supported by source, and says when the next rung on the ladder has been earned. SUBSET: rnv-publishing-agent and rnv-brand are not counted, so the floor is conservative by construction. Adding a repo to this list requires recomputing floor_observed in the same change.

tests._comment: Public surfaces carry a floor that steps in 5k increments, not an exact count. The exact figure came from a CI run and cannot be re-derived without running every suite; the floor can be, from source. Move the display to the next rung only when the source floor clears it.

eval_cases.note: Total only on public surfaces; the split is never published. A trap flipping out_of_corpus -> in_corpus on publication moves the split without moving the total, so the split fails the publication test and lives here as a machine-checked fact instead.

derive.note: Exactly derivable: one JSON object per line, each carrying a 'kind'. Frozen at 60 by decision 2026-08-05; update split in the same commit as any trap flip.

eval_thresholds._comment: The three gates. Declared in rnv-ask-the-corpus/eval/thresholds.json and quoted on the resume; the checker verifies the two agree. COVERAGE GAP, recorded 2026-08-09 rather than assumed away: resume/index.html prints all three percentages and repos['rnvizion.github.io'].checks does NOT include 'thresholds', so the site copy is declared here and verified nowhere. Values match today; a change to thresholds.json would go stale on that page silently. 'thresholds' is deliberately NOT added to that repo's checks -- the dispatch looks for eval/thresholds.json, which the site repo does not have, so it would fail spuriously. The real fix is a check that reads the printed percentages off the page; tooling chat.

expiring_surfaces._comment: Surfaces that go stale on a calendar rather than on a change. This is NOT a facts entry: facts assert that a surface matches a derived value, and this asserts that a date is still comfortably ahead of today. There is nothing to derive it from -- the file IS the source -- so the check is a comparison against now. Note the consequence: this is the one check that fires while the surface is still correct. That is deliberate; by the time it is wrong it is too late, because nothing else will ever prompt a refresh. WIRING, as of 2026-08-09: nothing reads this block yet. refresh_profile.py has no temporal check -- every other check is string matching -- and no repo's 'checks' array names an expiring group. Until that lands this is a declaration, not a guard, which is the same shape as facts.eval_cases sitting with an empty 'sources' array and being verified against nothing. Recorded here so the gap is visible from inside the file rather than discovered when the date passes.

.well-known/security.txt.reason: RFC 9116 makes Expires mandatory. An expired security.txt reads as an abandoned project, which is a worse signal than having no file at all. Weekly profile-drift gives roughly eight warnings before the fail window, which is enough notice to act without the warning becoming noise.

manual_surfaces.name: OpenSSF Best Practices Baseline
manual_surfaces._comment: Here rather than in facts{} for two reasons. Nothing in the repos derives it -- the figure lives on bestpractices.dev -- so no check_facts guard is possible. And OpenSSF owns the denominator: a control added or reclassified moves the claim with nobody touching a repo, which is the same drift class as a source count auto-incrementing. Deliberately NOT paired with the other two per-project figures: 46 tests (AIII, frozen by decision #4) and 786 tests / ~76% coverage (toolkit, complete) change only on a commit, so they are safe published and safe unguarded. Revisit if either unfreezes.
check: Control count still reads 20 of 21. The denominator is OpenSSF's, not ours, and can change without a repo commit
The unmet control is still the maintainer-review criterion, which a solo maintainer structurally cannot satisfy
Resume and site say 'an OpenSSF Best Practices Baseline submission at 20 of 21 controls' -- a submission at a count, never a passing badge. Keep that wording; it is the part that is precisely true
The one exception is still documented rather than hidden, which is the claim's actual load-bearing half
manual_surfaces.cadence: Check when a resume variant is next revised. That is when the claim gets re-read anyway, so attaching it to an existing event beats inventing a schedule nobody keeps.
